sentences.sentence: SpaceX planned to launch a Falcon 9 rocket from Kennedy Space Center at Cape Canaveral in Florida carrying the uncrewed Dragon cargo ship, but the launch has been postponed because the company found there was a problem with one of the rocket's engines.
The mission was originally supposed to launch on Thursday, but was postponed to allow the company to find and fix the problem.
The latest delay is so the company can make sure that they do not have another failure like the one they experienced two weeks ago when one of the engines failed during testing.
If all goes according to plan, the rocket should launch at 11.18am GMT (7.18pm EST) tomorrow.
But this isn’t just any rocket; this is the first rocket to try to be landed back on Earth after leaving it.
The Dragon cargo ship should leave Earth, but then the first stage of the Falcon 9 will come back and then land on the platform, a drone ship, named “Autonomous Spaceport Drone Ship” or ASDS.
But it's going to be a tough job, since according to CEO Elon Musk, the odds are only about 50-50.
If the rocket doesn't make it back, it will burn up in the air and fall into the ocean, which would be a loss for SpaceX, but not the end of the world.
However, if it does succeed, it would be a huge step in making space travel more economical and practical for more people.
For those hoping to see the launch, the rocket is expected to be visible from the Space Coast, Florida, and from parts of Georgia, Alabama and South Carolina, weather permitting.
